Causative Get and Have in the Active Pattern
The causative form is used when we don't perform an action by ourselves, and we arrange for somebody else to do it.

You can use causative get and have in active and passive voices.
When you use causative get and have in the active voice, it has the meaning of “cause or order someone to do something”.

The structure is:

get + person + infinitive (to + verb)
have + person + verb (infinitive without to)

Causative have:
Example:
My boss has me write his speeches.
Causative get:
Example:
My friends got me to make the presentation.

There is a slight difference in meaning between get and have in this structure. When you get someone to do something for you, it implies that you need to convince them in some way.
When you have someone do something, it means that you are giving the responsibility to someone else to do something.
When you use the get and have in a passive voice, it has the meaning of “arrange for someone else to do something”. You use this structure when you want to express that you pay or ask someone to do something for you.

The structures are:

get + object + past participle
have + object + past participle

For example:
I have to get my jacket cleaned.(It means that somebody else is going to clean the jacket.)
She has her guitar fixed in the city. (It means that somebody else fixes the guitar.)

When you use the passive, you come across less direct and therefore more polite.
I'll have your co-workers introduced to you tomorrow.

Modals to Express Necessity, Duty and Advice

When you want to express your opinion about what is right and what is wrong, you use the modals should and ought to.
You use the modals must, need and their negatives mustn't and needn't to talk about what is necessary and not necessary.

In a workplace setting, there are opportunities to discuss duties and to give advice to others.

For example:
You should take this job seriously. (= it's your duty)
Drivers ought to be more considerate on the road. (=it's their duty)
You really shouldn't be handing in reports late. (= strong advice criticism)

You need to make sure that the context of the comment is right, otherwise you come across as condescending and rude.

You use must and mustn't when you decide for yourself what is necessary.

For example:
You mustn't keep asking for my help all the time. (= I don't want you to)
I really must be going. (I think I must)

You can also use must and mustn't for impersonal necessity (something that is imposed upon you).

For example:
The screw must be tight for it to hold.

You use need and needn't to talk about something that is / is not necessary to be done.

You need to inform us about any emergencies that prevent you from being at work.
You needn't come to dinner if you don't want to. (In this example, the authority comes from the speaker).
You mustn't be concerned by that.

images.text:
Boris: And here we are back to your offices. Did Ms. Moore mention you would be sharing space with a few co-workers?
Kristi: Yes, she did.
Boris: Great. You mustn't be concerned by that. We want to promote a collaborative work environment. You ought to meet them as soon as possible. I'll have your co-workers introduced to you tomorrow.
Kristi: Oh, that's no problem at all.

Boris: How are your organizational skills?
Adam: Hmmm ... I'm not really sure.
Boris: You'll need to devote some time to establishing general organization techniques that work for you, such as how to arrange your files and who to contact for specific information. You should include some flexibility in your system.
Kristi: I understand.

Boris: Next, you will need to adopt planning strategies. As editorial assistants, planning is particularly important, especially in relation to project management. Projects get divided into many different tasks. Sometimes, each task has got to be completed before the next one can begin. You must plan your tasks ahead of time to bring the project to fruition. You mustn't lose track of any part of the project. It really helps to be detail-oriented. I'll have Ms. Moore talk to you more about that.
Adam: Ok.
Boris: You should try to make good use of scheduling. Scheduling involves allocating a time period for specific tasks or workload, and then assigning tasks. As we've mentioned before, this is a deadline-based industry. In order to respect due dates, effective time management techniques have to be used.
